methods.name: Peer-Median

data.narrative:
Kraftblock is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Martin Schichtel and Susanne König that has raised €20M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies across climate and energy, including 1 public company (Lanza Tech, ticker LNZA) and 8 private firms such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline of $20M and applying a typical Series B-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.9x, yields $38M. Peer-median benchmarking across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C)—produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $32M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $519M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Kraftblock's relative competitive position and technology maturity versus the peer set. Key variables affecting this range include product differentiation relative to Series C-stage peers, capital efficiency trajectory, and market adoption timelines in the decarbonization sector.
